solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Questioned former partner I named in break-up (8)

indicators.note: a break-up scatters the letters of I NAMED

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
I NAMED rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is grilled about an ex who got named in a messy break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a divorce story; 'break-up' is really the instruction to rearrange I NAMED.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine someone is to question them closely.

clue.text: Reorganise Venice’s exhibits (7)

indicators.note: reorganising puts the letters in a new order

blocks.note: the possessive is read as plain letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to rehang the art collections of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhibits' looks like a noun for gallery pieces; it is the verb, as in shows or displays. The apostrophe in Venice's is ignored, so its S counts.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to exhibit or show it.

clue.text: Separate section at end of article (5)

indicators.note: PART goes at the end, after A

blocks.note: the indefinite article
a section is a portion or piece of something

explanation.surface: Instructions for splitting off a section at the end of a written article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' is the grammar kind here, A, and 'at end of' simply puts the section after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: things set apart are kept separate from one another.

clue.text: Suspect incited associate in the same way (11)

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dodgy, so the letters of INCITED are not to be trusted as they stand

blocks.note: INCITED rearranged
an ally is an associate

explanation.surface: A suspect who stirred up trouble and an accomplice did it the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' reads as a noun, a person under suspicion; here it is an adjective telling you to rearrange the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Done identically means done in exactly the same way.

clue.text: Group of hard-bitten campaigners put up tents (6)

indicators.note: the answer is a group of letters taken from the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle the join: last two of 'hard-bitten', first four of 'campaigners'

explanation.surface: Tough veteran activists pitching tents for a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: The protest-camp picture makes 'Group of' look like a collective noun; it only marks a run of letters across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: To encamp is to set up a camp, which means putting up tents.

clue.text: Charged particle overcoming resistance in metal (4)

indicators.note: the ion comes over, i.e. wraps around, the R

blocks.note: an ion is a charged particle
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A physics note about ions overcoming the resistance of a metal conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: The electrical setting makes 'resistance' sound technical, and it is: R is its standard symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: iron is one of the metals, the commonest one in industry.

clue.text: Source of venison and caviare? Not cheap, we hear (3,4)

indicators.note: we hear marks both words as sounds rather than spellings

blocks.note: caviare is sturgeon eggs, the kind of fish eggs this word names
dear means expensive

explanation.surface: A menu musing that venison and caviare both come at a price.
explanation.walkthrough: Both luxury foods sit in the surface, but only 'venison' is the definition; caviare gives the first sound. Dear is British everyday for expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: venison is deer meat, and this small European deer is one species it comes from.

clue.text: Ingredient in gunpowder can upset Royal Engineers (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, reading it bottom to top

blocks.note: a tin is a can
RE is the army corps abbreviation

explanation.surface: Army sappers knocking over a can of gunpowder ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: The military setting disguises 'can' as a verb; it is the noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, potassium nitrate, is the oxidiser in gunpowder.

clue.text: Furious vegetarians lying about getting slimmer (5)

indicators.note: lying about means turned round, so the letters run backwards
the word is trimmed at both ends, leaving a slim run of letters

blocks.note: veg(ETARI)ans read backwards

explanation.surface: Angry vegetarians fibbing about losing weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' looks like fibbing; it means lying around, turned about.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone in a rage.

clue.text: Modern movement in the main? (7)

blocks.note: modern means of the present day, up to date
the main is the open sea

explanation.surface: A question about some new trend in mainstream thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the ocean, so a movement in it is a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Current means modern, and a current is water flowing in the sea.

clue.text: Recipient of legal statement about gift and contents of deed (11)

indicators.note: the contents of DEED are its inside letters

blocks.note: re means about, as in a letter heading
a present is a gift
d(EE)d

explanation.surface: Legal paperwork about a gift, with a deed attached.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal vocabulary spills from the definition into the wordplay, so 'deed' seems to belong to the definition when it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a representee is the person to whom a representation, a statement of fact, is made.

clue.text: Reduced share (3)

blocks.note: reduced means made smaller, trimmed back
a share is someone's portion of the takings

explanation.surface: A reduced shareholding.
explanation.walkthrough: Two plain senses sit side by side: an adjective for something made smaller and a noun for a portion of the spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: the past participle of trimming something down, and the slang noun for a person's portion of the proceeds.

clue.text: Watch for one article in US magazine? (9)

blocks.note: Time is the American news magazine
a piece is a written article

explanation.surface: A wry idea that a watch is just a piece in Time magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' usually gives A or THE; here it is a newspaper-style article, a piece. The whole clue reads as a pun: a Time piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a watch is one kind of clock-like device for telling time, hence 'for one'.

clue.text: Pain caused by running fast: it chafes to some extent (6)

indicators.note: only part of the words is used

blocks.note: the letters straddle the colon: the end of 'fast', all of 'it', the start of 'chafes'

explanation.surface: A runner complaining of pain as their kit rubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chafes' fits the runner's aches so well that the letters hiding across the colon are easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp pain in the side brought on by running.

clue.text: Fashionable, affected teens characterised by deep feelings (7)

indicators.note: affected means altered, so TEENS changes its order

blocks.note: in means fashionable
TEENS rearranged

explanation.surface: Trendy, posturing teenagers full of big emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' reads as posturing, fitting the teenagers; it is the signal to rearrange TEENS.
explanation.definitionFit: An intense person is marked by strong, deep feelings.

clue.text: Valley is home to English boy (6)

indicators.note: the gorge houses the E inside it

blocks.note: a gorge is a steep valley
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English boy growing up in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English boy' looks like one unit, but English gives only E and 'boy' alone is the definition; George is simply a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: it is a common boy's name, so 'boy' stands for any name a boy could have.

clue.text: Regularly repair electrical connection for noise-suppressing device (7)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, every second one

blocks.note: r(E)p(A)i(R)
a plug makes an electrical connection

explanation.surface: Routinely fixing the wiring of a noise-suppressing gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' reads as how often you repair things; it picks out every other letter of 'repair'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: the device is pushed into the ear canal to suppress noise.

clue.text: Run framework to assist climbers? (6)

blocks.note: a run is a line of unravelled threads in tights or stockings
rungs set in a frame for climbing

explanation.surface: A question about some structure for climbers to use.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a ladder is a run, a line of unravelled threads, in tights or stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder is both a run in hosiery and a climbing frame.

clue.text: Consumer holding back about counter-attack? (9)

indicators.note: EATER holds TAIL inside it
about means turned round, so the whole thing is read backwards

blocks.note: an eater consumes
the tail is the back end

explanation.surface: A shopper hanging back before hitting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a reversal signal but is the letters TAIL; the reversal comes from 'about'. Counter-attack here is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to hit back after being attacked is to counter-attack, with counter-attack read as a verb.

clue.text: Millions supporting existing monarchy? (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporter sits underneath, so M goes below REAL

blocks.note: real means actually existing
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Millions of people backing a monarchy that still exists.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is royalist politics; 'supporting' only places M beneath REAL in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, the territory of a monarch.

clue.text: Boozer’s naked after dropping ecstasy (3)

indicators.note: dropping means letting something fall away, so the E falls out of BARE

blocks.note: bare means naked
E is slang for the drug ecstasy, and is removed

explanation.surface: A drinker ends up naked after coming down from ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' looks like a drinker, but in British slang a boozer is a pub. The 's means is.
explanation.definitionFit: A boozer, in British slang, is a pub or bar.

clue.text: One book containing nothing for flipping pancakes (5)

indicators.note: the pair I B contains NIL
flipping turns the result over, reading it backwards

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
nil is nothing
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A cookbook with no advice on tossing pancakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping pancakes' reads as tossing them in the pan; flipping is the reversal of I-NIL-B, and 'pancakes' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: these are small buckwheat pancakes from Russian cooking, one particular kind of pancake.

clue.text: Displeased by anodyne broadcast (7)

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, like seed

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A listener put out by a bland radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the radio picture; its older sense, sown far and wide, is what scatters the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone irritated or put out.

clue.text: Hearing test (5)

blocks.note: a court hearing
a test is an experiment to see if something works

explanation.surface: A hearing test at the audiologist.
explanation.walkthrough: The ear-test picture points at sound; 'hearing' is the courtroom kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a court hearing of a case, and an experimental test, as in a trial run.

clue.text: Assemble leaders from most employers each time (4)

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters

blocks.note: M(ost) E(mployers) E(ach) T(ime)

explanation.surface: Company bosses gathering whenever most employers do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' suggests bosses in the business setting; it means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: people who assemble come together, as at a gathering.

clue.text: Raising awareness of how to behave (8)

blocks.note: raising animals means rearing them for offspring
awareness of how to behave is good manners from an upbringing

explanation.surface: Campaigning to teach people good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising awareness' reads as one campaigning phrase; the split falls after 'Raising'.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeding is raising animals, and also the good manners of a proper upbringing.
